name: opentide
description: The opentide workbench for detection engineering: live checks for Tide objects and their KQL, SPL, ES|QL, EQL, Kibana KQL, Lucene and Falco queries, templates, catalogue, ATT&CK coverage, query results and deploy previews.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: In Restricted Mode only the language server runs, from the bundled runtime. Commands, tasks, panels, MCP and the workspace's own opentide need a trusted folder.

virtualWorkspaces.description: In a virtual workspace (github.dev, vscode.dev, Remote Repositories) only highlighting, languages and language configuration work: opentide reads the workspace from disk.

opentide.path.markdownDescription: An `opentide` executable (run with `lsp start`, every feature) or an `opentide-lsp` executable (run with `--stdio`, editor features only). Used before any other runtime. Ignored in Restricted Mode.

opentide.interpreter.markdownDescription: A Python interpreter with opentide installed. When set, it replaces the Python extensions, `.venv` and `PATH` lookup for the workspace runtime. Ignored in Restricted Mode.

enumDescriptions: The first runtime that answers: `opentide.path`, the workspace's environment, uv with the repository's pin (when `opentide.uv.usePin` is on), then the bundled runtime.
Always the runtime bundled with the extension.
opentide.runtime.markdownDescription: Which opentide runtime the extension uses.

opentide.uv.usePin.markdownDescription: Run the opentide version the repository pins (`pyproject.toml`, `requirements*.txt`, `uv.lock`) with `uv tool run --from opentide==<pin>`. Tried before the workspace's environment. Ignored in Restricted Mode.

opentide.uv.path.markdownDescription: The `uv` executable for `opentide.uv.usePin`. Default: `uv` on `PATH`. Ignored in Restricted Mode.

opentide.envFile.markdownDescription: A `.env` file, relative to the workspace folder, whose variables are passed to commands that contact a tenant (opentide reads credentials only from the environment). Ignored in Restricted Mode.

enumDescriptions: Use one warm `opentide serve` process when the runtime has it.
opentide.backend.serve.markdownDescription: How the extension runs opentide commands.

opentide.trace.server.markdownDescription: Traces the communication between VS Code and the opentide language server, in the `opentide Language Server Trace` output.

enumDescriptions: Provide the opentide MCP server to VS Code's agents, unless the workspace's `.vscode/mcp.json` already defines `opentide`.
Always provide it; VS Code shows one `opentide` server when a workspace file defines one too.
opentide.mcp.provide.markdownDescription: Whether the extension gives VS Code's agents the opentide MCP server (`opentide mcp start` with the resolved runtime, the bundled one included). Off in Restricted Mode, where this setting is not read.

enumDescriptions: Validate the saved object file (`opentide validate --file`). Saving a configuration file validates the workspace.
Validate the whole workspace on every save.
Only when you run opentide: Validate Workspace.
opentide.validate.onSave.markdownDescription: When `opentide validate` runs on save, in the `opentide validate` problems. The language server checks open files as you type either way.

opentide.validate.onStartup.markdownDescription: Validate the workspace in the background when the extension starts, so problems in files you have not opened show up too.

enumDescriptions: Lint the saved object file (`opentide lint --file`), when the active opentide has that option.
Only when you run opentide: Lint Workspace.
opentide.lint.onSave.markdownDescription: When `opentide lint` (file names, recommended metadata, placeholders, query style) runs on save.

opentide.lint.withValidate.markdownDescription: Lint the workspace whenever the workspace is validated (on startup, on Validate Workspace, and on save with `opentide.validate.onSave` set to `workspace`).

opentide.query.lenses.markdownDescription: Show **Run**, **Validate live** and **Compiled query** lenses above each query in a rule and in query files.

opentide.query.defaultWindow.markdownDescription: The look-back a query run offers first (`--since`): `15m`, `24h`, `7d` or ISO-8601 (`PT1H`).

opentide.query.retainResults.markdownDescription: Keep a query's last results in memory after its panel closes, for this window. Results are never written to disk except by **Export**.

opentide.terminal.addToPath.markdownDescription: When the bundled runtime is active and no `opentide` is on `PATH`, put the bundled `opentide` on new integrated terminals' `PATH`. Ignored in Restricted Mode.

languageModelTools.name: opentide_open_file_diagnostics
languageModelTools.userDescription: The problems VS Code shows for a file: the language server's, opentide validate's and lint's.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns every diagnostic VS Code currently shows for one file, merged across the opentide language server, `opentide validate` and `opentide lint` (and other extensions), with severity, source, code, message and 1-based line/column ranges. Use it for the live state of a file the user is editing, including unsaved changes the language server has checked. Defaults to the active editor's file. For workspace-wide validation, use the opentide MCP server's tools instead.

file.description: An absolute path, or a path relative to the first workspace folder. Omit for the active editor's file.

languageModelTools.name: opentide_active_object
languageModelTools.userDescription: The Tide object in the active editor, its UUID and what it connects to.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns the opentide object (threat, objective or rule) open in the active editor: its UUID, type, schema, name, TLP, platforms, techniques and tactics, why its file did not load (load_error) when it did not, and its graph neighbourhood one hop away (the objects, signals, ATT&CK techniques and log sources it points to or that point to it, with the edge kind and field path). Use it to learn what the user is looking at. For the whole catalogue, search or validation, use the opentide MCP server's tools instead.

colors.description: Background of a line whose value is an `opentide new` placeholder (`# opentide:placeholder`).
Overview ruler mark of a placeholder line.

args.description: Arguments after the command, such as ["--strict"] or ["--platform", "sentinel"].

walkthroughs.title: Get started with opentide
walkthroughs.description: From an empty folder to a validated detection, its ATT&CK coverage and a deploy preview.

steps.title: opentide is ready
steps.description:
The extension bundles opentide, so it works without installing Python. The graph and the ATT&CK matrix need a newer opentide than the bundled one. The status bar shows which opentide runs.
[Show the Runtime](command:opentide.statusMenu)
[Use My Environment's opentide…](command:opentide.switchRuntime)

steps.title: Set up a detection repository
steps.description:
A wizard over `opentide setup`: platforms, CI, agents and hooks. Review lists every file before anything is written.
[Set Up Repository…](command:opentide.setup.open)

media.altText: The setup wizard's Review step, listing the files opentide setup will create or merge.

steps.title: Create your first detection
steps.description:
Start a rule from a template, then step through its placeholders with Next Placeholder (Ctrl+Alt+.; Ctrl+Alt+, goes back).
[New Rule…](command:opentide.setup.step?%5B%22create%22%5D)

steps.title: Validate it
steps.description:
Problems fill as you type; Validate checks the whole repository as CI does.
[Validate Workspace](command:opentide.setup.step?%5B%22validate%22%5D)

steps.title: See how it fits
steps.description:
The graph shows what the rule implements; the ATT&CK matrix shows what the repository covers.
[Show the Graph](command:opentide.setup.step?%5B%22graph%22%5D)
[Open the ATT&CK Matrix](command:opentide.setup.step?%5B%22matrix%22%5D)

media.altText: A threat, its objective and two rules, and the ATT&CK technique they cover.

steps.title: See how it fits
steps.description:
The graph and the ATT&CK matrix show what each rule implements and what the repository covers. They need an opentide with `info catalog`, newer than the one running now: use a newer opentide in the repository's environment, or set opentide.path.
[Use My Environment's opentide…](command:opentide.switchRuntime)

media.altText: A threat, its objective and two rules, and the ATT&CK technique they cover.

steps.title: Preview a deploy
steps.description:
A dry run: what each rule would send to each tenant, sending nothing.
[Preview a Deploy](command:opentide.setup.step?%5B%22deploy%22%5D)

steps.title: Bring your agent
steps.description:
MCP is on for VS Code agents: the extension provides opentide's MCP server. For Cursor, Claude Code and other hosts, and to install the opentidehq/skills Agent Plugin (recommended), use Bring Your Agent…
[Bring Your Agent…](command:opentide.setup.agents)
